Secretive

/SEE-krih-tiv/ - the stress falls on SEE · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Secretive means tending to keep one's thoughts, plans, or activities hidden.

Our secretive neighbor waves hello every morning but has never once said what hums away all night in the workshop behind his house.

Worked Example

No one at the reunion could say what Aunt Petra had done for a living. Forty years of holiday cards mentioned 'work travel' without a city or a job title, and direct questions met a smile and a refilled glass. She wasn't cold—just so secretive that her own sisters had long ago stopped asking.

Secretive describes the person and the habit, not a single act: everyone conceals something sometimes, but the secretive person hides ordinary things—plans, whereabouts, opinions—as a settled way of living.

How Secretive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tight-lipped

tight-lipped: unwilling to talk about a particular subject

uncommunicative

uncommunicative: giving little away in conversation, whatever the reason

Antonyms

open

open: sharing thoughts and plans freely

forthcoming

forthcoming: volunteering information readily

How Strong Is It? — private → secretive → underground

private vs. secretive

private vs. secretive: Private people keep some matters to themselves, as everyone may; secretive goes further—a settled habit of hiding even ordinary doings.

underground vs. secretive

underground vs. secretive: Underground outdoes secretive: a secretive person hides their business while living in the open, but an underground network hides its very existence.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of secretive.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — se-

Prefix — se-: apart

Root — cret

Root — cret: sifted, set apart (from Latin cernere)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to

Put it together

Put it together: Se- (apart) + cret (sifted, set apart) + -ive (tending to) = tending to set things apart. Latin secretus meant 'separated out'—what is secret has been sifted away from common view. A secretive person runs that sieve constantly, sorting life's ordinary details into the hidden pile.

Use the root in a new word: certain

Use the root in a new word: certain: After checking the map twice, she was certain of the turn—the question was settled in her mind.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, mildly disapproving

Secretive labels a person or organization whose habit is hiding. Its unit-mates divide the scene: conceal is the act of hiding one thing, surreptitious describes a single action done to escape notice, and evasive is how a secretive person often sounds under direct questioning. Private is the kinder cousin—use it when the hiding is a reasonable boundary rather than a suspicious habit.
